gpt.text:
Run the three “Next Commands” in the order shown; that sequence is coherent:

1) **AUB autopilot (select-best)**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```
- Purpose: execute module-level AUB experiments and (if the tool is configured to do so) update/mark the best-performing module candidate.
- What to capture after it finishes:
  - which candidate (if any) was selected as “best”
  - the resulting tuning/lockbox mean+min deltas vs `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`
  - any failures/timeouts (these often explain “no PASS candidates” situations)

2) **System autopilot**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
- Purpose: evaluate end-to-end/system-level candidates listed in `system_candidates.yaml`.
- What to capture:
  - PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE summary
  - per-candidate metrics and where the run artifacts/logs were written

3) **Generate next-fix report**
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
- Purpose: produce a prioritized “what to fix next” markdown based on latest experiment outcomes.
- Expected output: `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` (commit or attach it to the handoff).

### Quick sanity checks before/after running
- Confirm the champion file exists and is the one you intend:
  - `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`
- If you keep seeing “no PASS candidates,” the next-fix report is usually the most actionable artifact—generate it even if system autopilot fails.

### If you paste anything back here
Paste:
- the console summary from each command (last ~50–100 lines is usually enough), and
- the contents (or key sections) of `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`.

I can then help interpret why there were no PASS candidates and suggest the most promising candidate/module to focus on next.
